question: The concept of "Republic" in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**France.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Republic"** refers to a **form of government** where the head of state is** not** a **monarch,** but a **president **or other elected official.
 
• India adopted the concept of "Republic" in its Constitution on **January 26, 1950**, when it became a **sovereign democratic republic.**
 
• The Constitution of India was largely influenced by the Constitutions of the** United States, the United Kingdom, and France.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Germany** did not have a republican form of government until after **World War II.**
 
• **Australia** became a republic only in **1999, **while India adopted the concept of Republic in 1950.
 
• **Japan **has a **constitutional monarchy,** where the **Emperor** is the** symbolic head of state.**
 
• **France **was the first country to adopt the **Republican form **of government during the **French Revolution in 1792.**
